evidence: The Black Ark's TEAC four-track is attested by Perry in interviews and by musicians and engineers who worked there, and it recurs in every detailed account of the studio. Accounts differ on the exact model suffix and on what else was in the room at which date.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen to the rhythm under Murvin's high voice. It is dense and slightly blurred, as if heard through gauze. Drums, percussion and guitar melt into one texture instead of standing apart. Each time Perry combined finished parts onto one track to make room for more, another layer of hiss and softness went on. The haze is what four tracks cost, spent on purpose.

explanation.age7: Lee Perry made famous records on a home tape recorder with only four tracks.
explanation.age13: Most professional studios had many more tracks than this machine's four. Lee Perry kept filling them up, squashing them together onto one track, and recording more. That made his records sound thick and hazy, and people still try to copy that sound on purpose.
explanation.adult: The constraint produced the style. Generational loss from repeated bouncing is audible across the Black Ark's output, and it separates those records from the cleaner multitrack productions of larger Kingston studios in the same years.
